title: GitHub - magenable/magento-adobe-commerce-mcp-server: Magento Open Source and Adobe Commerce MCP server
snippet:
# Magento Open Source / Adobe Commerce MCP Server
This is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that connects to a Magento Open Source or Adobe Commerce REST API making possible Claude, OpenAI Agent Builder and other MCP clients to request supported Magento REST API endpoints. This server support both local and remote HTTPS connection.
## Benefits
- **Broader API coverage (read + write):** enables agents to not only retrieve data, but also update content and product data when appropriate.
- **Multi-store aware:** supports working across multiple store views / websites from a single MCP connection.
- **Compact responses (default):** returns lean payloads to reduce token usage and, in turn, LLM costs.
- **SearchCriteria support for advanced querying:** enables complex filtering/sorting/pagination for “data mining” style requests.
- **Secure remote connectivity (HTTPS):** supports connecting agents over the internet (e.g., Agent Builder / remote MCP usage).
## Installation and running:
1. Install [nodejs](https://nodejs.org/en) 20 and above
2. Create Integration access token via admin interface of your Magento Open Source/Adobe Commerce store
```
System -> Extensions -> Integrations -> Add new integration
```
3. Clone this repo
```
git clone git@github.com:magenable/magento-adobe-commerce-mcp-server.git
```
4. Go to workdir
```
cd magento-adobe-commerce-mcp-server
```
5. Install dependencies
```
npm install
```
6. Copy and fill .env
```
cp .env.sample .env
```
7. Generate JWT Token
```
npm run jwt:generate username
```
8. Starting HTTP server
```
npm run start:http
```
or use [pm2](https://pm2.keymetrics.io/)
```
pm2 start "npm run start:http" --name mcp-magento
```
OpenAI need HTTPS connection and domain. You can use NGINX as a reverse proxy and install a certificate, for example, via certbot

### Connect with OpenAi Agent Builder
- Login to platform.openai.com
- Go to [https://platform.openai.com/agent-builder](https://platform.openai.com/agent-builder)
- Edit Workflow
- Add MCP workflow module
- Add server
- Configure connection

title: Freento MCP Server  - User Guide
snippet:
Freento MCP Server is a module for Magento 2 that enables integration between a Magento store and AI assistants
that support the Model Context Protocol (MCP), such as ChatGPT, Claude, and other compatible AI tools. The module
provides a standardized and secure way for AI assistants to access Magento data for querying, analysis, and reporting.
The MCP server functions as an intermediary layer between Magento and AI clients. It exposes a set of read-only
tools that allow AI assistants to retrieve structured data from the store, including orders, products, customers, inventory,
marketing rules, and system information. All data access is performed in real time and is limited to the permissions explicitly
granted through Magento’s access control system.
Freento MCP Server is designed with security and operational safety as core principles. It uses OAuth 2.0
authentication with role-based access control, supports separate credentials for each AI client, and does not store or
replicate store data outside Magento 2. Sensitive information such as passwords and payment details is never exposed.
This approach allows merchants, sales and marketing teams to safely use AI-driven analytics and automation while
maintaining full control over data access and compliance requirements.

Requirement
Version
Magento
2.4.x (Open Source or Commerce)
PHP
8.1 or higher
AI Client
Claude Code, Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, or any AI tool with MCP support
Extension Installation
Step 1: Install the Extension
From GitHub repository:
composer require freento/module-mcp
Or manually: Download and extract to   app/code/Freento/Mcp/
Installation from Commerce Marketplace
1.​ Login to your account at Commerce Marketplace
2.​ Go to “My Purchases” section
3.​ Follow the instructions in the “How to Install” section
Step 2: Enable the Module
Run the following commands from your Magento root directory:
php bin/magento module:enable Freento_Mcp
php bin/magento setup:upgrade
php bin/magento cache:flush
Step 3: Verify Installation
php bin/magento module:status Freento_Mcp
Expected result:   Module is enabled

consists of two mandatory steps:
1.​ Creating an ACL Role
2.​ Creating an OAuth Client
These steps are required for both CLI-based AI tools and web-based AI assistants.

snippet:
# Adobe Commerce Dev MCP Server
This project implements a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that interacts with Adobe Commerce. It provides tools to search the GraphQL and REST API schemas, and prompts to help write and validate API integrations.

## Usage with MCP Server via NPM Package
You can use this MCP server directly without downloading or hosting anything yourself. Simply configure your MCP client (such as Cursor or Claude Desktop) to use the NPM package:
```
{ "mcpServers" : { "adobe-commerce-dev-mcp" : { "command" : " npx " , "args" : [ " -y " , " @rafaelcg/adobe-commerce-dev-mcp@latest " ], "env" : { "ADOBE_COMMERCE_VERSION" : " 2.4.8 " } } } }
```

- Replace the server name (`adobe-commerce-dev-mcp`) as you wish.
- The `npx` command will always use the latest version of the MCP server from NPM.
- Set `ADOBE_COMMERCE_VERSION` to match your store (`2.4.7` or `2.4.8`). Defaults to `2.4.8`.
- No need to install or host anything locally or remotely.
On Windows, you might need to use this alternative configuration:
```
{ "mcpServers" : { "adobe-commerce-dev-mcp" : { "command" : " cmd " , "args" : [ " /k " , " npx " , " -y " , " @rafaelcg/adobe-commerce-dev-mcp@latest " ], "env" : { "ADOBE_COMMERCE_VERSION" : " 2.4.8 " } } } }
```

## Version configuration
The `ADOBE_COMMERCE_VERSION` setting controls which schema files are loaded by both tools and which version is referenced in prompts.
| Method | Example | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `env` in MCP config | `"ADOBE_COMMERCE_VERSION": "2.4.7"` | Claude Desktop, Cursor, production |
| CLI argument | `ADOBE_COMMERCE_VERSION=2.4.7` in the Arguments field | MCP Inspector |
Supported versions: `2.4.7`, `2.4.8` (default).
> **REST schema fallback:** if the REST schema file for the configured version is not found, the server falls back to `2.4.8` and includes a note in the tool response.

## Development
The server is built using the MCP SDK and communicates with Adobe Commerce.
1. `npm install`
2. Modify source files
3. Run `npm run build` to compile
4. Run `npm test` to run tests
5. Add an MCP server pointing to the built file (see below)
**Local MCP config:**
```
{ "mcpServers" : { "adobe-commerce-dev-mcp" : { "command" : " node " , "args" : [ " /absolute/path/to/adobe-commerce-dev-mcp/dist/index.js " ], "env" : { "ADOBE_COMMERCE_VERSION" : " 2.4.8 " } } } }
```
**MCP Inspector:**
```
npm run inspector
```

# Model Context Protocol (MCP)
The Magento PhpStorm plugin can expose Magento-specific IDE tools through JetBrains MCP.
You can use these tools with Codex, Junie, Claude Code, Cursor, and other MCP-compatible assistants.
Plugin version 2026.3.5 requires a JetBrains IDE from the 2026.2 line or newer (build 262.8665.265 or later). Install and enable the Magento 2 and Adobe Commerce plugin, open your Magento project, and check its Magento settings. If `Settings | Tools | MCP Server` is missing, make sure the IDE's bundled MCP Server plugin is enabled.
In WebStorm and other IDEs without the PHP plugin, your assistant can find modules, DI declarations, observers, layouts, UI components, and ACL and menu entries. CLI environment and magerun discovery are also available. Finding plugins that intercept a particular method, generating Magento code, and running compatibility checks require a PHP-capable IDE.
## 1. Enable the IDE MCP server
Open `Settings | Tools | MCP Server`, enable `Enable MCP Server`, and confirm the warning dialog.
![](./images/mcp/4_enable_mcp.png)
## 2. Check exposed Magento tools
Open `Settings | Tools | MCP Server | Exposed Tools` and make sure the Magento tools you need are enabled. Look for tools such as `magento_inspect`, `describe_magento_cli_environment`, and `magento_magerun`. In a PHP-capable IDE, `magento_scaffold` and `magento_compatibility` are also available. Available tools depend on your plugin version and IDE.

### External assistant
For an assistant running outside JetBrains AI Assistant, open `Settings | Tools | MCP Server`. Under `Clients Auto-Configuration`, click `Auto-Configure` for your client, then restart it. If your client is not listed, use `Manual Client Configuration` and follow its instructions for adding an MCP server. See the [JetBrains setup guide](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/phpstorm/mcp-server.html#external-client-setup).
### Codex in JetBrains AI Assistant
1. In `Settings | Tools | MCP Server`, copy the HTTP Stream configuration from `Manual Client Configuration`.
2. Open `Settings | Tools | AI Assistant | Model Context Protocol (MCP)`, add an HTTP server, and paste the configuration. Click `Apply`.
3. Open `Settings | Tools | AI Assistant | Agents` and enable `Pass custom MCP servers`.
4. On the MCP Server settings page, click `Auto-Configure` for Codex, save your settings, and restart the client if needed.

# Adobe Commerce / Magento MCP
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool for integrating with the Magento REST API. No direct SQL or server access required.
## Supported Editions
This MCP tool is compatible with:
- **Adobe Commerce (formerly Magento)**: Enterprise-grade eCommerce platform with advanced features and support.
- **Magento Open Source**: The free, open-source edition of Magento, suitable for small to medium businesses.
All features are implemented using the official Magento REST API, ensuring compatibility and security for both editions. No direct database or server access is required—just API credentials from your Magento instance.

### 3. Configure
Create or edit your `.cursor/mcp.json` file and provide your Magento/Adobe Commerce instance credentials:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"adobe-commerce-mcp": {
"command": "node",
"args": ["/path/to/adobe-commerce-mcp/build/index.js"],
"env": {
"COMMERCE_BASE_URL": "https://your-magento-instance/",
"COMMERCE_CONSUMER_KEY": "your_consumer_key",
"COMMERCE_CONSUMER_SECRET": "your_consumer_secret",
"COMMERCE_ACCESS_TOKEN": "your_access_token",
"COMMERCE_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET": "your_access_token_secret"
}
}
}
}
```
### 4. Run
Start the MCP server as defined in your configuration. The tools will be available for use in any MCP-compatible client or workflow.

title: MCP Server
snippet:
**Freento MCP Server** connects your Magento 2 store to AI assistants via the https://modelcontextprotocol.io/ - an open standard for AI-to-application integration. Once connected, AI can query your store data in natural language: "show me revenue by month", "find customers who haven't ordered in 90 days", "which products are low on stock".
The module provides a set of read-only tools covering different areas of your store:
- Sales - orders, order items, quotes (including abandoned carts), quote items, credit memos
- Catalog - products with attribute filtering, inventory/stock levels
- Customers - customer accounts with filtering by email, group, dates, store
- Marketing - cart price rules, coupons
- Admin - admin users with roles, locked accounts (failed login detection)
- System - Magento, PHP, MySQL, Redis, OpenSearch/Elasticsearch versions

**Security & Access Control**
- OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE
- Role-based ACL: choose exactly which tools each AI client can access
- Multiple OAuth clients with independent permissions
- All data stays in your Magento database - no external storage, no data duplication
- Read-only access - the module cannot modify store data
**Works with**
- Claude Code and Claude Desktop (bearer token via .mcp.json)
- ChatGPT and web-based clients (OAuth 2.0 flow)
- Any MCP-compatible AI tool
The module is also available on Github with full source code, user guide, and issue tracker. Please refer to the [Github repo](https://github.com/Freento/Magento-2-Mcp) for detailed setup and usage instructions.

### Adobe Commerce platform compatibility
**Adobe Commerce (cloud):** 2.4 (current)
**Adobe Commerce (on-prem):** 2.4 (current)
**Magento Open Source:** 2.4 (current)

### 1.2.0:
- ** Compatible with Adobe Commerce (cloud) :** 2.4
- ** Compatible with Adobe Commerce (on-prem) :** 2.4
- ** Compatible with Magento Open Source :** 2.4
- **Stability:** Stable Build
- **Description:**
## v1.2.0
**Anonymity Mode** — New privacy setting under Stores → Configuration → Freento → MCP → Privacy. Hides personal data fields (emails, names) in admin-related responses. New ACL resource `Freento_Mcp::config` for role-based access.
**Multi-Aggregation Queries** — Aggregation API now accepts multiple aggregate functions in one call; `group_by` supports array format; output reformatted to one line per group.
**Improvements** — `get_locked_admins` adapts to Anonymity Mode; fixed Knockout checkbox bindings; introduced `SchemaFactory`
